text:
support-bot: @channel Customer escalation: multiple customers reporting p95/p99 regressions on /v1/generate since ~12:30 UTC. Topline: p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s, p99 up to 3.4s. Affected: hosted-us-west-2, model redwood-std-13b and some 70b slots under dedicated. Example request_id=req_0a9f3c, seen at 2026-03-15T12:34:02Z. Logs attached in support ticket #4521. :warning:

maya: seeing the alert too. Grafana shows a sudden tail increase on tokenization and kernel queue times around 12:29-12:36. Not all regions impacted. Can someone pull the per-GPU queue length and batch sizes?

josh: pulling logs now. Quick note: a recent deploy at 12:15 introduced new batching heuristics (dynamic batching threshold). Rolling back in my head as a suspect.

leah: copying the trace for req_0a9f3c: ``TRACE req_0a9f3c: enqueue->batch_wait(180ms)->kernel_queue(840ms)->decode(140ms)``. Kernel queue is the big chunk. GPU utilization for the pod was low (43%) during the spike, but nvlink contention high on that node.

samir: nvlink contention + longer kernel queue often means one of: a) unexpected slow host path (IO/PCIe) b) heterogenous kernel selection causing suboptimal kernels. I'm going to check the kernel selector logs.

ops-bot: Deploy event: service/serve-runtime v3.12.1 rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T12:15:08Z by josh. Canary 10% -> 100% by 12:26.

maya: thanks. josh, can you confirm whether the new batching threshold change touched kernel hints? If so, reverting to previous heuristics might help.

josh: it did. I modified the threshold to be more aggressive (aimed to reduce latency) which increases batch size. In some workloads that increases kernel queue wait because kernels pick suboptimal paths for larger batches. Rolling back now to v3.12.0 canary -> full rollback staged.

tina: escalation from a customer (Acme Payments): their p99 hit 3.8s and they are threatening to throttle usage. We should offer immediate mitigations: per-customer circuit breaker, fallback to smaller model, and regional routing to eu-west-1 if that region is healthy.

leah: mitigation plan sequence I recommend:
1) Immediate: enable per-customer short-circuit circuit breaker for customers with >80th percentile latency spike (30s window).
2) Fallback: route that customer's requests to redwood-lite-6b (quant) model in a healthy region (eu-west-1) via routing policy.
3) Short-term: revert batching heuristic (josh rollback).
4) Mid-term: pin kernel selection to safe kernels for affected model->hw combos while we debug selector.

maya: adding concrete commands. To enable circuit breaker via admin API (temporary):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/admin/circuitbreakers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"customer:acme","metric":"p95","window_seconds":30,"threshold_ms":1000,"action":"failfast"}'
```
This will short-circuit new requests >1s p95 to return 503 quickly so customer app can fallback.

samir: also add a routing override: route requests from Acme to eu-west-1 redwood-lite-6b:
```json
{"policy":"route","match":{"customer_id":"acme"},"destination":{"region":"eu-west-1","model":"redwood-lite-6b-quant"}}
```
I can push that to the routing table now.

ops-bot: Routing change queued: rule id rt_993 will be applied in 30s if not canceled.

josh: rollback in progress: v3.12.0 -> full rollout. Watching canary + pod restarts.

leah: repro steps for SRE/REPRO team to validate locally:
1) Replay request with same token length and headers: ``curl -H "X-Request-ID: req_0a9f3c" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" --data-binary @payload.json https://hosted-us-west-2.redwood.ai/v1/generate``
2) Run the microbench script to stress batcher: ``./tools/batch-sim.sh --model redwood-std-13b --concurrency 160 --seq 1024``
3) Collect kernel selector debug: set env ``REDWOOD_KERN_DEBUG=1`` on a canary node and repro.

maya: I'm starting the replay on a repro cluster with env debug flags. If we can reproduce kernel_queue hang, we can pin kernels.

support-bot: Customer notified: "We’ve activated temporary protections (short-circuit + fallback) while we investigate. We will update within 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:

samir: kernel-selector logs show a fallback to a generic kernel path for large batches around 12:28 which is slower. There is also a spike in agentd IO retries to the model shard storage at the same time (latency ~120ms per shard read vs baseline 5ms). That explains low GPU util + long kernel queue: workers waiting on IO and then draining queue in big bursts.

josh: that points to a storage IO regression. Any recent infra changes? Storage team, ping if you're here. @storage-team

ops-bot: Alert: Block device error rate increased on host i-0a7f2a in us-west-2 from 12:20 to 12:40 — diagnostic ticket stg-880 opened.

tina: OK. Given storage is implicated, keep the circuit breaker + fallback. Also add a unit-level rate limit: reduce per-customer token rate to 60% for 15 minutes to reduce amplification while storage is investigated.

maya: applying rate limit now via admin throttle API:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/admin/throttles" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"acme","type":"token_rate","scale":0.6,"duration_seconds":900}'
```

ops-bot: Throttle rule applied: thr_220 active.

leah: quick checklist for SLO guardrails we want post-mortem actioned:
- set automatic circuit-breaker for p95>800ms for 60s window.
- auto-fallback policy to smaller model/region if kernel_queue >500ms observed on 3+ nodes.
- synthetic traffic ramp to detect storage IO regressions earlier.
- dashboard: per-customer p95/p99 with circuit-breaker state and routing overrides.

josh: rollback finished; canary looks healthy. I'll wait 5m and then measure tail latency again.

maya: repro cluster shows the same IO spikes when we hammer shard reads. Storage team confirm degraded EBS performance on the particular AZ. Switching route to eu-west-1 nodes eliminated the kernel_queue spikes in our test.

samir: long-term fix ideas: (a) add local prefetching for hot shards to avoid synchronous reads in hot paths; (b) make kernel selector prefer streaming-friendly kernels when IO latency is high; (c) expose a storage health signal to routing so we can proactively divert.

tina: Customer update: Acme accepted fallback to eu-west-1 redwood-lite-6b for next 2 hours and appreciates quick automation. Billing note: we should not bill at reduced SLA for that window; support will open a credit.

support-bot: Action items assigned:
- josh: follow up with infra/storage (ticket stg-880) and confirm host replacement or migration.
- samir: add kernel pinning quick patch for redwood-std-13b while selector fix is developed.
- maya: run post-mortem draft and SLO guardrail RFC with checklist from leah.
- leah: add automated synthetic that hits shard reads aggressively for warm-up (dev task).

maya: tagging this thread for postmortem writing. I'll start the timeline and include traces + the rollout diff for v3.12.1 -> v3.12.0 rollback.

josh: current numbers (12:55 UTC): p95 back to ~210ms for affected customers in us-west-2; p99 ~480ms. Continuing to monitor for 30m.

ops-bot: Monitoring check: no new deploys detected. Storage ticket stg-880: host i-0a7f2a marking for replacement; migrating shards.

support-bot: closing loop: customer notified of credit and fallback. Will reopen if tail reappears. Thanks team. :pray:, great coordination.
